findings.shape: A distinct slender, solid-spotted cheetah artist body replaces no existing species. The 25-joint runtime hierarchy articulates pelvis, lumbar/thoracic regions, neck/head, tail and four three-segment limbs. The source tail/neck proportions, hip volumes, face and toe anatomy remain unmeasured and partly stylized.
findings.surface: Retained original UV atlas and source image bytes. Short tapered hairs inherit the same surface colors and skin weights. Eighteen separate oversized hooked white claws were shortened and toned down at runtime using author-selected factors, guided by authentic photographs and the Smithsonian description of blunt semi-retractile claws. No photographic pixels were painted into invented anatomy. Exact fur optics, individual markings and claw dimensions remain unmeasured.
findings.movement: A finite lateral four-foot stepping study has independently grounded stance/recovery intervals, forward trunk progression, modest authored trunk lowering, recovery paw pitch and subtle spine/tail articulation. It stops after 4.2 display seconds. Source-pose fitting, higher carpal landmarks and continuous chain-coordinate skin weights replaced an initially overconstrained/folding wrist solution. A separate bounded head turn returns to the original pose. Gallop, prey handling, repose and sleep remain unavailable.
changes: Retained hendrikReyneke’s credited cheetah surface and atlas, with unchanged source/delivery GLB bytes.
Added connected-limb segmentation so adjacent right fore/hind paws do not inherit each other’s weights.
Authored a 25-joint pelvis/spine/head/tail/four-limb hierarchy and bounded lateral stepping with separate support and recovery.
Corrected shoulder/carpal placement, reachable support targets and paw orientation after failed support tests and actual screenshots.
Replaced discontinuous height-based skinning with continuous chain-coordinate blending after a close-up revealed an open-looking carpal crease.
Shortened 18 exaggerated hooked claws and added a short-fur surface derivative; original source file retained.
Added authentic walking, face and lateral-body photographs with exact creator, license, source and actual derivative/delivery checksums. Rejected a footprint-only candidate as a body photograph.
Preserved all 306 earlier species objects, including the wolf/tiger surfaces and action paths.
remaining: Exact head/eye/lip, tail/neck proportions, shoulder-blade anatomy, pads and fine digits remain incomplete or unmeasured.
Short fur and coat colors are qualitative artist derivatives, not calibrated optical or photo-matched surfaces.
Only a bounded walking study and local head turn are implemented; continuous gait, galloping/aerial phases, prey acquisition/ingestion, repose and physiological sleep remain unfinished.
No fitted animal trajectories, forces, contact deformation, energetics, respiratory physiology, population-wide dimensions or independent specialist validation are established.
This single admission is 5 of 50 requested new large animals after deployment verification; 45 remain. Other incomplete archive mechanisms are not marked complete.

softwareScope: Targeted taxonomy/provenance, preserved payload, stance/clearance, constant long-bone lengths, reset and welded-surface checks pass. Full regression/build/compiled/publication checks are separate gates.
iterationHistory: Initial support checks failed with fixed short carpal offsets. A subsequent freely articulating chain gave an unsuitable wrist fold in actual captures. Corrected carpal landmarks, controlled support geometry and paw pitch passed; close-ups then exposed abrupt skin-weight blending. Continuous chain-coordinate weights and explicit seam checks replaced that draft. Oversized hooked claws were subsequently reduced, and the final support checks passed again. The first full suite also found two metadata-format mismatches (Bundled GLB delivery wording and lowercase uncalibrated timing), corrected without weakening the checks.
